headline: Proposed public dog park on Spine Road, with paved parking near the Nashua River, was toured; decisions come later.
summary: Issues raised included dog waste, park hours, and lighting. Possible Blanding turtles and a falcon were noted, and possible conditions include invasive plant removal, native plantings along fencing, and educational signs.
plain_text:
DRAFT MINUTES 
CITY OF NASHUA 
CONSERVATION COMMISSION  
November 23, 2026 
Dog Park Spine Rd.  
______________________________________________________________________________ 
 
The site walk was called to order at 4:00 by Chair Dutzy    
Roll call by: Commissioner Dutzy 
Those Present:  Commissioners: Sherry Dutzy, Richard Widhu, Brandon Pierotti, Carol Sarno. 
Commissioner Darby arrived prior to adjournment.,    
 
Others Present:  James Petropulos, IMEG;  Matt Sullivan & Levent Akinci, Nashua Community 
Development; Liz Hannum, Nashua Economic Development; Amber Morgan, Nashua Alderwoman; 
Members of the Mine Falls Advisory Committee: Ben Davis, Andrew & Natalie Iucci, and Paula 
Lochhead; Shana Demers, Professor Rivier University; Mya Blanchard, Reporter, Nashua Ink Link, 
Jarrod Williams, Hooksett; Roger Lochhead, Nashua interested environmentalists.  
_________________________________________________________________________ 
THE FOLLOWING SITE WALK MUST ONLY DISCUSS THE PROPERTY LISTED.  A BRIEF DESCRIPTION AND INFORMATIONAL 
WALK WILL BE CONDUCTED BY THE OWNER AND/OR HIS REPRESENTATIVE. DISCUSSION CONCERNING BUFFER   IMPACTS 
AND ANY RELATED TOPICS ON THE SUBJECT PROPERTY WILL BE COVERED.  THE WALK SHOULD THEN ADJOURN WITH NO 
FURTHER DISCUSSION OF CONSERVATION BUSINESS. ALL DECISIONS WILL BE MADE AT AN UPCOMING MEETING AND 
POSTED ON THE AGENDA ACCORDINGLY.  SITE WALK NOTES /MINUTES WILL BE APPROVED AT THAT TIME. DRAFT 
MINUTES NEED TO BE MADE AVAILABLE WITHIN ONE WEEK OF THE WALK.  
 
The purpose of the site walk was to view city-owned property which is being proposed for a public dog 
park. Amenities to the property entail encroachment of the 75’ prime wetland of the Nashua river to 
create a paved parking area (8 spaces) and paved access road along with a pergola for shade and 
seating. This project is a public/private partnership with Mr. Petropulos representing the developer. 
 
The area to be disturbed was flagged. It is flat and grassy with old pavement extending from Spine Rd. 
The entire area is in a floodplain, therefore development options are limited The river embankment is 
shrubby and has glossy buckthorn and bittersweet present.  Gaps in the fencing were noted. Mr. 
Petropulos noted that a pipe is being planned as part of the drainage management plan. Runoff will be 
treated prior to entering the existing outlet to the Nashua river.  
 
A tall antenna with guide wires is located to the NE of the proposed dog park. A falcon was seen 
perched at the top. Mr. Williams works nearby, frequents the area, and is involved with the Audubon 
Society in efforts to re-nest the bird for its safety. Although the dog park project doesn’t involve 
removal of the antenna, once it is decommissioned the City may want to dismantle it. Members of the 
groups noted that they had no problem with it remaining. Maintaining the falcon habitat is critical. 
 
Issues raised were as follows: 
1) Plan to remove dog waste so as not to foul the river; City stated that a plan is being worked out 
2) Park hours: city noted it would be dawn-to-dusk as other parks unless special events were held 
3) Lighting: Plan is for lighting around the pergola for safety at present. This could change. All 
lighting is Dark Skies approved. 
4) Future development that could further erode wildlife habitat. To be discussed further. Possible 
Conservation Easement? 
5) Does the parking area need to be asphalt? Due to possible flooding, it is felt that a porous 
surface will not hold up.
Professor Demers mentioned the possible presence of Blanding turtles. She noted that dogs and turtles 
do not get along and suggested that a dense zone of native plants be planted along all fencing for turtle 
protection. She also suggested signage and that this was a good opportunity to educate the public about 
the wildlife present. Jarrod Williams thought it possible for New England cottontail to also be present.  
 
 
Possible stipulations are as follows:  
1) Removal and proper disposal of glossy buckthorn, bittersweet and other invasives found along 
the embankment. 
2) Dense native plantings along all fencing to protect turtles 
3) Develop a waste removal plan 
4) Educational signage about possible endangered wildlife activity  
 
As there were no further questions, Commissioner Sarno moved to adjourn. Seconded by 
Commissioner Widhu. The meeting adjourned at 4:38 PM. 
 
Submitted by:     Date: 
Sherry Dutzy     November 23, 2026
